inconsistencies: #35713 and #35139 attack the same problem (replacing Boost.Test macros with in-tree, thread-safe assertions). Review #35713 first; #35139 is an explicit NOMERGE sketch and should be judged as feedback on #35713's assertion design rather than independently.

Chain: #36916 (BSD ephemeral-port collision fix) is stated as unblocking #36147 (native FreeBSD CI). Review #36916 first; #36147 also carries a temporary commit disabling other CI jobs that must be dropped.

#36729, #36730 and #36846 all come from the same forced socket-chunking investigation (#36724 / #36726 / #36751). Review them as one batch, starting with #36730 because it fixes the framework transport rather than a single test.

Platform-CI overlap: #35774 (macOS arm64 binaries), #36082 (Guix release binaries) and #36147 (FreeBSD) all add 'run tests on binaries we currently never execute' coverage. #36082 partly subsumes #35774's macOS binary testing; decide the intended end state before merging both.
#32554 supersedes the earlier #32457 attempt to replace the static block fixture; the older approach should be closed rather than reviewed in parallel.
#36794, #36831 and #36923 are all test-isolation cleanups serving issue #36692 and can be reviewed together under one decision about the desired fixture style.

Stated prerequisites that fix review order: #36786 builds on #36765, #35911 is based on #36087, #36808 is based on #36844, #35442 depends on #35433, #36936 depends on #35756, #36843 is draft pending unspecified prerequisites.
#34360's value is contingent on #27865 (separating spent from spendable outputs); if that optimization is not pursued, the benchmark loses most of its justification.
#36587, #36937 and #36916/#36147 are all BSD-family platform test failures; a reviewer with BSD access should take them as a group.
result.notes: No P1 in this category: nothing here leaves a correctness or fund-safety defect in the product unresolved; the strongest items are CI-signal and high-risk-coverage work. The P2 band is reserved for (a) framework-wide signal fixes, (b) fuzz/unit coverage of consensus and p2p paths currently unreached, and (c) platform or harness changes that remove a recurring burden or catch regressions that already merged undetected. Single-test flake fixes, speedups, added benchmarks and ordinary coverage adds sit in P3; pure style, include and annotation churn sits in P4.
